name: Seattle
tax_rate: City special hotel-motel tax not imposed; 7% King County convention and trade center tax inside Seattle; 2.3% STIA fee at 71 downtown hotels
notes: No city LTAC grant program found; Seattle lodging taxes go to the Washington State Convention Center and the STIA fee goes to Visit Seattle marketing.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue Tax Reference Manual: Convention Center Taxes
funding_docs.summary: Describes the King County convention and trade center tax (7% inside Seattle, 2.8% elsewhere in King County) that funds the Washington State Convention Center; this is where Seattle lodging tax goes rather than to a city grant program.

funding_docs.title: Hotel and Lodging Tax in Seattle 2026 (Roommaster summary)
funding_docs.summary: Secondary summary showing Seattle's combined 15.7% lodging rate, no city special hotel-motel tax imposed, and the 2.3% STIA fee at 71 downtown hotels that funds Visit Seattle marketing.

pool_note: No city lodging tax fund: the 7% convention center tax inside Seattle is a King County/state levy committed to Washington State Convention Center debt and the STIA fee goes to Visit Seattle, so nothing is open to outside applicants.

name: Bellevue
tax_rate: 5.5% city transient occupancy tax (grandfathered) plus $2.50/night TPA fee
notes: 100% of Bellevue's lodging tax passes to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority (Meydenbauer Center) under an agreement running to 2034, so there is no open LTAC application.

funding_docs.title: City of Bellevue 2021-2022 Adopted Budget, Economic Development proposals
funding_docs.summary: States that 100% of Bellevue's transient occupancy (lodging) tax passes through to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority under an operating agreement running to 2034, paying Meydenbauer Center bonds, capital reinvestment and part of operations.

funding_docs.title: Bellevue Ordinance 5005 (hotel/motel tax)
funding_docs.summary: City ordinance governing Bellevue's special hotel/motel tax; no outside grant process is created by it.

pool_note: Revenue figure not published; per the 2021-22 budget 100% of the city's lodging tax passes through to the Bellevue Convention Center Authority through 2034, leaving nothing for outside applicants.

name: SeaTac
deadline_pattern: Around May 31 of the second year of each biennial budget; off-cycle requests due 10 days before a regular Hotel Motel Advisory Committee meeting (2nd Wednesday)
contact: Maria Langbauer, Senior Economic Development Strategist, mlangbauer@seatacwa.gov
notes: Only municipalities, PFDs and 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) nonprofits are eligible; reimbursement-based; the special hotel/motel tax brought in about $2.06M in 2025.

members.name: Byron Pihuave
members.affiliation: Cedarbrook Lodge (seat listed vacant on March 11, 2026 agenda)

presentation.pattern: Hotel Motel Advisory Committee reviews applications at its regular monthly meetings; off-cycle requests are heard at the meeting following the 10-day submission cutoff; whether applicants present is not stated

meeting_schedule: Second Wednesday of each month, 3:00 pm, SeaTac City Hall

funding_docs.title: 2026/27/28 SeaTac Lodging Tax Funding Application
funding_docs.summary: Application and instructions for the 2027-2028 biennial cycle due May 29, 2026; eligible uses are tourism marketing, special events and tourism facility operations or capital, open only to municipalities, PFDs and 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) nonprofits, paid on reimbursement.

funding_docs.title: HMAC meeting packet, March 11, 2026 (agenda, Feb 11 minutes, lodging tax distribution report)
funding_docs.summary: Shows special hotel/motel tax receipts of $2.16M (2023), $2.15M (2024) and $2.06M (2025) and the 2027/28 application timeline.

funding_docs.title: HMAC meeting packet, June 12, 2024 (2025-2026 funding request summary)
funding_docs.summary: HMAC-recommended 2025-2026 awards totaling about $1.45M including WA Brewers Guild ($107K-$112K/yr), Museum of Flight ($100K/yr), The Roadhouse and Highline Botanical Garden ($112K-$116K/yr); estimates $2.2M/yr revenue and a $12.9M fund balance.

funding_docs.title: HMAC meeting packet, November 13, 2024 (2025/26 application, scoring sheet, June 24 minutes)
funding_docs.summary: Scoring results for 2025/26 requests: SeaTac BMX capital and programming, Seattle Southside RTA shuttle, meetings and BMX incentives, and City TDDP implementation recommended; Highline Heritage Museum, Channel A TV and Highschool GG not recommended.

pool_note: Estimate: 2025 special hotel/motel tax receipts were $2.06M; the HMAC-recommended 2025-26 awards to outside organizations (WA Brewers Guild, Museum of Flight, The Roadhouse, Highline Botanical Garden, NW Symphony) total roughly $690K per year, with the remainder going to Seattle Southside RTA programs, city TDDP implementation and a $12.9M fund balance.

name: Spokane
deadline_pattern: Two rounds per year: late March (events July-June) and early-mid October (2025 round due Oct 10 for January-June events)
typical_open: March 1 for the spring round; mid-September for the fall round
notes: Run as Tourism and Cultural Investment (TACI) grants through the Neighborly portal; nonprofits, for-profits and public agencies can apply, up to $10,000 per organization.

presentation.pattern: TACI committee reviews written applications submitted through the Neighborly portal after each deadline and notifies awards about 4 weeks later (April 27, 2026 for the March round); no applicant presentation is described

funding_docs.title: TACI Grant Flyer 2026
funding_docs.summary: Announces the spring 2026 round (open March 1, due March 31) with grants up to $10,000 per organization for events held July 2026 through June 2027.

funding_docs.title: TACI Grant Workshop Presentation, March 2026
funding_docs.summary: Technical assistance deck covering eligibility, the Neighborly portal and scoring for the 2026 TACI round.

funding_docs.title: TACI Committee minutes, November 21, 2025 (Spring 2026 awards)
funding_docs.summary: Committee approved $81,000 for 15 spring 2026 grants plus $5,000 for Bloomsday's 50th, awards ranging $2,500-$10,000 with the largest $10,000 to The Family Guide, Blue Door Theatre and MasterClass Big Band Foundation.

funding_docs.title: FAQs for TACI Grant Application
funding_docs.summary: Explains the twice-yearly application rounds, that nonprofits, for-profits and public agencies may apply, and that the committee recommends awards to City Council.

pool_note: Revenue not published; the Nov 21, 2025 TACI minutes awarded $86,000 across 16 outside grants for the spring 2026 round (max $10K each), and a second round of similar size runs each fall.

name: Tacoma
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax; 5% at properties with 26+ rooms (includes 3% convention center tax)
notes: No City of Tacoma LTAC application found; Tacoma is not in the Pierce County LTAC grant program, and the city's Special Events Funding ($90K, due Oct 21, 2025 for 2026) is paid from venue food-and-beverage tax, not lodging tax.

funding_docs.title: WA Department of Revenue: Tacoma lodging tax rate change notice (July 2021)
funding_docs.summary: Lists Tacoma lodging taxes: 5% special hotel/motel tax at 26+ room properties (13.6% combined) and 2% at 25 or fewer rooms (12.3% combined).

funding_docs.title: City of Tacoma 2026 Special Events Funding announcement
funding_docs.summary: The city's only open event grant program: $90,000 to 28 organizations at $2,500-$5,000 each for free public events, funded by Tacoma Dome and Convention Center food-and-beverage tax, not lodging tax.

pool_note: No City of Tacoma lodging tax grant program was found and lodging tax revenue is not published; the city's $90K Special Events Funding comes from venue food-and-beverage tax, so lodging tax dollars open to outside applicants are 0.

name: Vancouver
deadline_pattern: Around September 20 each year for the following calendar year; LTAC reviews in Oct-Nov, Council approves in December
contact: Andrew Westlund, Economic Development Management Analyst, andrew.westlund@cityofvancouver.us
notes: Four grant types (Cultural Enrichment up to about $5K, Large Event/Festival for 2,500+ attendees, Tourism Program/Facilities, Tourism Organization Operating); requires a 501(c)(3)/(c)(6) host or fiscal sponsor.

presentation.pattern: LTAC reviews applications in October and November, about 3 to 8 weeks after the September 20 deadline, and sends recommendations to City Council in December; applicant presentations are not described

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Committee Grant Program Guidelines (2026 update, for 2027 cycle)
funding_docs.summary: Four categories: Cultural Enrichment targeted at $5,000 or less, Large Event/Festival typically $10,000-$25,000 (past awards up to $95,000), Tourism Program/Facilities ($15,000-$40,000 past program awards) and Tourism Organization Operating ($1M-$1.3M/yr to the DMO); no match required, scoring favors overnight stays, off-peak and outside-downtown events.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Advisory Grants Flyer 2027
funding_docs.summary: One-page notice: applications open Aug 4 and close Sept 20, 2026, with a virtual Q&A Aug 19.

funding_docs.title: LTAC Budget Memo (FY 2025)
funding_docs.summary: Lodging tax revenue of about $3M/yr (3.7M in 2023); 50% is committed to Convention Center debt service and about $1.5M/yr is available for LTAC grant awards, with $6.3M cash reserves and a $2.9M debt guarantee.

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Grant Program page (links to 2026 award recommendations and scoring rubric)
funding_docs.summary: Program page listing the 2026 award recommendations, scoring rubric and partnering-with-hotels guide; LTAC reviews in Oct-Nov and Council approves in December.

pool_note: Estimate: FY2025 memo shows about $3M/yr revenue with 50% to Convention Center debt and about $1.5M for LTAC awards, but the Tourism Organization Operating grant to the DMO takes $1M-$1.3M of that, leaving roughly $200K-$500K for outside events, programs and facilities.

name: Redmond
deadline_pattern: Early-to-mid August each year for the following calendar year (2027 cycle due Aug 10 at 5 p.m.)
contact: Jackie Lalor, Economic Development & Tourism Program Administrator, 425-556-2209
notes: Open to public or private organizations; grants may not exceed 50% of project cost and must attract overnight visitors.

presentation.pattern: Staff score written applications and LTAC adopts funding recommendations at a meeting about 3 weeks after the August deadline (Sept 1, 2026; Aug 26, 2025); agendas list no invited applicants

meeting_schedule: Roughly quarterly on a Tuesday afternoon at Redmond City Hall with a call-in option (2026: Feb 24, Apr 27, Jun 2, Sep 1)

funding_docs.title: 2027 Tourism Promotion Program Application
funding_docs.summary: Application due Aug 10, 2026 at 5 p.m.; grants may not exceed 50% of project cost and must bring overnight visitors to Redmond; late submissions not accepted.

funding_docs.title: LTAC agenda, September 1, 2026 (2027 Tourism Grants funding recommendations)
funding_docs.summary: Meeting at which LTAC adopted its 2027 tourism grant funding recommendations for Council; the agenda itself does not print the award table.

funding_docs.title: LTAC minutes, August 26, 2025 (2026 grant recommendations)
funding_docs.summary: LTAC approved $175,000 in 2026 event grant recommendations 6-0 after a record number of applications, including $17,000 to Surf Cup and $5,000 to Young Professionals Theater, with $25,000 available above staff recommendations.

funding_docs.title: LTAC minutes, April 27, 2026 (2027-2028 budget priorities)
funding_docs.summary: Sets the event grant line at roughly $175,000/yr (a $25,000 add was one-time) and $30,000/yr for strategic marketing partnerships, with more advertising investment under discussion.

pool_note: Revenue not published; LTAC approved $175,000 in 2026 event grants to outside applicants (Aug 26, 2025 minutes) and budgets about $175K/yr for 2027-28 plus $30K/yr in strategic marketing partnerships.

name: Kirkland
deadline_pattern: Varies year to year; 2026 grants were due June 1, 2026 and earlier cycles were due in late July (2024) and August (2025)
contact: Jen Davis Hayes, Economic Development Manager, jdavishayes@kirklandwa.gov, 425-587-3038; tourism@kirklandwa.gov
notes: Run by the Tourism Development Committee for events that draw visitors from 50+ miles; the city page says the 2027 application period is closed, but the 2027 due date is not posted.

presentation.pattern: Tourism Development Committee reviews applications at its monthly meeting roughly a month after the deadline (July 2, 2026 for the June 1 deadline); applicant presentations are not described

meeting_schedule: First Thursday of the month (2026: Feb 5, Mar 5, Apr 2, May 7, Jul 2, Aug 6)

funding_docs.title: Tourism Events Grant Funding program page
funding_docs.summary: Grants for marketing or operations of events that draw visitors from 50+ miles and generate overnight stays; $110,000 awarded for 2026 with reimbursement requests due Dec 15, 2026.

funding_docs.title: 2025-2026 Outside Agencies and Tourism Funding issue paper (2025-26 budget)
funding_docs.summary: TDC recommended a $694,704 tourism budget for 2025-2026 from the 1% lodging tax, with a $60,000 annual grant program; for 2025 it recommended $60,000 across ten organizations against $98,300 requested.

funding_docs.title: City news release: 2026 Explore Kirkland tourism grants (April 14, 2026)
funding_docs.summary: Announces about $60,000 in 2026 grants for marketing and operations, applications due June 1, 2026 at noon.

pool_note: 2025-26 budget sets a $694,704 biennial tourism budget (about $347K/yr) from the 1% lodging tax, most of it Explore Kirkland staffing and marketing; $110,000 was awarded to outside events for 2026 against a published $60K annual grant line.

name: Everett
deadline_pattern: Mid-December for the following calendar year; awards announced by end of January
contact: Tyler Chism, Placemaking Program Manager, tchism@everettwa.gov, 425-257-7107
notes: Nonprofits and public agencies can apply, and for-profits can join through a nonprofit or public sponsor; operations are prioritized and marketing-only requests go to the Snohomish County TPA.

presentation.pattern: Written applications submitted through Euna are scored by LTAC in January, with awards announced by end of January; no interviews or presentations

meeting_schedule: As needed; the 2026 LTAC meeting was February 12, 2026 at 2 pm

funding_docs.title: LTAC 2026 Info Guide
funding_docs.summary: $200,000 pool for 2026; applications open Nov 3 and close Dec 15, 2025 via Euna; operations prioritized, marketing-only requests referred to the Snohomish County TPA; nonprofits and public agencies eligible, for-profits via a sponsor.

funding_docs.title: Resolution 8283: approving LTAC recommendations for 2026 lodging tax allocations
funding_docs.summary: Council adopted $200,000 in 2026 awards recommended Feb 12, 2026, including Cruzin' to Colby $16,000, AMGRAF gallery season $12,000, Eventuris 3on3 $11,000, Downtown Everett Association $10,000, Downtown Flower Program $6,000 and 4th of July Parade $5,000.

funding_docs.title: Resolution 8137 (2025 lodging tax allocations)
funding_docs.summary: Prior-year council resolution adopting the LTAC's 2025 lodging tax award recommendations.

pool_note: Revenue not published; Resolution 8283 adopted the LTAC's $200,000 in 2026 grant awards to outside organizations, the full published pool.

name: Tukwila
deadline_pattern: Rolling; due by noon on the second Thursday of a month for that month's LTAC meeting (fourth Tuesday, 1 p.m.)
contact: Brandon Miles, Business Relations Manager, Brandon.Miles@tukwilawa.gov, 206-431-3684
notes: Only government entities and nonprofits are eligible, and applications need visitor projections; contracts over $40K need City Council approval.

presentation.pattern: Applications received by noon on the second Thursday are reviewed at that month's LTAC meeting on the fourth Tuesday; whether applicants present is not stated

meeting_schedule: Fourth Tuesday of each month, 1:00 pm, rotating City locations

funding_docs.title: Lodging Tax Funding program page
funding_docs.summary: Rolling applications from governments and nonprofits for events, marketing and tourism facilities funded by the 1% lodging tax, reviewed monthly by LTAC; contracts over $40,000 go to Council.

funding_docs.title: 2025 LTAC Application (blank)
funding_docs.summary: Application form requiring visitor and overnight-stay projections for each request.

funding_docs.title: City of Tukwila 2023-2024 Biennial Budget, Lodging Tax Fund (Fund 101)
funding_docs.summary: Hotel/motel tax budgeted at $720,000 (2023) and $750,000 (2024); spending of about $940,000/yr including $250,000 sponsorships, $50,000 advertising, $50,000 marketing and $375,000 contracted services, with a $1.6M-$1.8M fund balance.

pool_note: 2024 budget projects $750,000 hotel/motel tax revenue against about $945K in Lodging Tax Fund spending ($250K sponsorships, $375K contracted services, $100K advertising and marketing, staff); no award list separates outside grants from the city's own Experience Tukwila and RTA spending, so the competitive share is unknown.
